newsitem.title: USA: British M&As down 17 pct in 1996 to $96.7 billion.
newsitem.headline: British M&As down 17 pct in 1996 to $96.7 billion.

text.p: Mergers and acquisitions involving British companies fell 17 percent in 1996 to 1,610 transactions worth $96.7 billion, compared with 1,658 deals in 1995 worth $113.2 billion, according to data compiled by Securities Data Co.
For all European targets, mergers or acquisitions for the year totaled $248.4 billion on 4,765 deals, compared with less than $224 billion on 5,551 deals in 1995.

The biggest British deal was Sun Alliance Group Plc's $3.8 billion acquisition of Royal Insurance Holdings Plc. N.M. Rothschild & Sons advised Sun on the transaction, while Baring Brothers & Co advised Royal Insurance.
The Sun deal was far smaller than the largest European -- and global -- merger or acquisition of 1996: Sandoz AG's $30 billion union with Ciba-Geigy AG.
J.P. Morgan and UBS advised Ciba-Geigy on the deal, while Morgan Stanley advised Sandoz.

Britian's second-largest merger or acquisition for 1996 was Rentokil Group Plc's $3.1 billion acquisition of BET Plc. Its third-largest was Swiss Reinsurance's acquisition of Mercantile and General Reinsurance from Prudential Corp Plc for $2.72 billion.
SBC Warburg advised the most British deals for the year -- 46, valued at $18.7 billion. UBS was second with $18.3 billion and 29 deals.
Among all European targets, Morgan Stanley led financial advisors with 39 completed transactions valued at $55.9 billion.
Deals involving non-U.S. targets comprised only three of the year's top 24 deals, Securities Data said.
